parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or trans identity, and no documented visitor targeting, detention, facility or border regime, keep this above universal-exposure tiers. Against that, the 2024 cabinet/ministry direction to ban LGBTQ advocacy, framing of the community as contrary to values, church/official/chief opposition, conservative climate and advice to avoid public affection create a hostile official and social posture. Recourse is thin: no SO/GI discrimination law, only narrow teaching-service and digital-communication exceptions, and prosecutorial guidance weighing hostility toward prosecution is documented but a 2016 account showed only one lesbian-violence prosecution and near-invisible court presence. Unknowns on documents, facilities, custody, care and the committee's output prevent a higher score.

entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented refusal or marker regime for visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: Marriage amendment's effect on existing marriage or markers is not sourced; resident marriage law does not itself govern visitor entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Not documented. No documented arrests or custody placement for trans visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Same-sex conduct is not criminalised; no trans-specific criminal offence is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Absence of documented detention cannot be treated as proven safety in a thin dossier.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No bathroom, hostel, ward or other facility rule is sourced.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No subnational variation is documented; national findings cannot be assumed uniform locally.

care_services.exposure: Not documented. No care denial, medication or ward-placement evidence.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2024 cabinet decision and ministry committee direction to draft a policy banning LGBTQ advocacy/promotion, framing the community as contrary to constitutional, religious and regional values.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Prosecution Policy 2003, Prosecutors Code 2017 and vulnerable-witness principles require disregard of sexual preference and treat SO/GI hostility as weighing toward prosecution; 2011 UN joint statement signed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing targets advocacy/promotion rather than documented private conduct, but visitors lack resident standing and the committee's legal form/enforcement is unknown.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No minor-specific entry, care, custody or guardianship rule is sourced.
minors_guardians.protection: Same-sex partners receive no Family Protection Act 2008 protection and must use penal-code routes, per 2016 workshop.
minors_guardians.interaction: Marriage non-recognition and partner non-protection are mainly resident/family law; no specific traveller-with-minor exposure is documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Conservative climate, church/official/chief opposition at advocacy founding, advice to avoid public affection and no active gay scene; no documented pattern of anti-trans violence against visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented pattern of visitor violence; penal-code routes remain for offences.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Only one prosecuted violence-against-lesbians case and near-invisible LGBTI court presence in 2016 indicate recourse is rarely invoked.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general discrimination protection on SO/GI or employment basis; narrow Teaching Service Act 2013 and Harmful Digital Communications Act 2024 s2(2)(j) exceptions only.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Prosecutorial guidance is the clearest victim-side protection.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Application frequency of guidance, committee outcome, and subnational differences are unsourced; thin/uncertain recourse limits the rating.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than 0.35-B: that anchor has routine police stops, confiscations, fines and ineffective courts for visitors; here no visitor stops, detention pattern or trans-specific penalty is documented.
Higher than 0.55-B: that anchor has universal secondary screening, discretionary entry refusal and slow appeals for every trans visitor; here no such entry or screening exposure is documented.

Lower than 0.65-A: that anchor has explicit national equality protection, release ordered by courts and apology/compensation after questioning; here there is no equality law, official advocacy-ban framing is active, and prosecutorial recourse is rarely invoked.

Materially below 0.75-C: that anchor has respectful documented border practice, training and a tribunal with counsel and compensation; here no such operative visitor protections are documented and state framing is hostile.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is non-criminalising but officially unsupportive: private conduct is not documented as criminal, yet advocacy is targeted nationally in 2024, social opposition is conservative, and remedies depend on prosecutorial discretion rather than anti-discrimination law. No tier-1 universal exposure (border, facility, custody or care rule) is documented, so the case sits above 0.55 anchors, but thin, rarely-invoked recourse and hostile state framing keep it below 0.65 anchors where protections demonstrably operated. Undocumented document, facility, custody and care factors are treated as unknowns, not safety.
